key_insight: Controllable latent audio diffusion can be made much more compute-efficient by moving guidance into a small set of latent-control modules and applying selective, low-cost feature guidance (TFG), avoiding expensive decoder backpropagation while retaining fine-grained control.
problem_solved: Existing guidance-based controls for generative audio are either tied to costly model retraining or require expensive per-step decoder backpropagation during inference, making fine-grained controllability impractical for low-resource or real-time use.
method: Introduce Latent-Control Heads (LatCHs): lightweight plug-in heads attached to the latent space to receive and apply guidance signals directly without backpropagating through the full decoder.
Apply selective TFG (targeted feature guidance): restrict gradient- or signal-based guidance to targeted latent features or heads, minimizing per-step computational cost.
Combine LatCHs + selective TFG at inference to achieve effective control with far fewer backprop operations and lower latency compared to standard decoder-guided approaches.
impact: This approach lowers the compute and latency barrier for controllable audio generation, enabling interactive or resource-constrained workflows (e.g., real-time editing, mobile deployment) and making controllable diffusion more accessible to researchers and practitioners.

paper_title: Low-Resource Guidance for Controllable Latent Audio Diffusion
paper_authors: Zachary Novack, Zack Zukowski, CJ Carr, Julian Parker, Zach Evans
